citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel Fpz (frontopolar, the largest linear drift of the montage), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- subset from the SAME 64-channel root the Welch/Hjorth/spectrogram/coherence cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_fpz_s002r02) -> PhysioPreprocess::detrendSignal(type='linear'): subtracts the least-squares line. The reference re-computes both the linear and constant detrend with scipy.signal.detrend (a bit-exact check) and quantifies the spectral leakage -- the sub-1-Hz Welch power of the raw, linear-detrended, and constant-detrended signal -- via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the single frontopolar channel Fpz of the eyes-closed EEG, subset from agent/eval/data/hjorth-eeg/eeg64_s002r02.rds; Fpz has the largest linear drift of the montage (frontopolar channels pick up slow drift and EOG). Detrending is the quiet first step of almost every spectral analysis. This is the FIRST external-reference (scipy) certification of the detrendSignal primitive (previously 'golden' internal only). detrendSignal reproduces scipy.signal.detrend BIT-FOR-BIT: 'linear' (least-squares line via stats::lm.fit) to ~1e-12, 'constant' (mean) exactly 0 -- the formulas are identical. The finding is a real methodological point: on the drifting Fpz channel the sub-1-Hz Welch power falls from 1284 (raw) to 59 after LINEAR detrend but only to 112 after CONSTANT (mean) detrend, so the linear trend contributes ~47% of the low-frequency power that mean-removal leaves in -- the detrend TYPE matters for any low-frequency spectral estimate (this is the same detrend step the Welch/spectrogram cases rely on). Linear detrend removes only the LINEAR part of the drift; oscillatory wander needs a high-pass filter.
